A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of global kinetics models calibrated to steady burning data is a viable approach to predict the burning of composite solid propellants.

the calibration of a global kinetics model is feasible and that a model calibrated to a large set of homogeneous burning data can be used to predict three-dimensional, unsteady deflagrations of heterogeneous propellants with reasonable accuracy.
the calibration of a simplified global kinetics model is a necessary step in the development of an accurate simulation tool for composite solid propellants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calibration of global kinetics models based exclusively on homogeneous, steady burning data is a necessary first step toward accurate simulations of the deflagra-tion of solid propellant grains.
a global model that reproduces a large number of experimentally observed burning characteristics can also be used for three-dimensional simulations of the deflating of composite propellant grains.

, in the case of composite propellant burning, the calibration of global kinetics models is a nontrivial task that requires careful selection of the set of performance characteristics to be matched, and it is strongly influenced by the size of the parameter space to be explored.
